conditions.name: Common cold (upper respiratory tract infection)

triage.label: Self-care
triage.action: This can usually be managed at home

conditions.summary: A self-limiting viral infection of the nose and throat. Blocked and runny nose, sneezing, mild sore throat, and a cough that appears a few days in.
workup: Review if symptoms last beyond 10 days or fever returns

exam.positive: Their presence points away from streptococcus

labs.confirms: A low score supports a viral cause

conditions.name: Viral pharyngitis

triage.label: Self-care
triage.action: This can usually be managed at home

conditions.summary: The commonest cause of a sore throat by far. Comes with a cough, runny nose and hoarseness, which is precisely what distinguishes it from strep.
workup: Review if unable to swallow fluids

exam.positive: Normal, or scattered wheeze clearing with cough
Focal crackles or dullness point to pneumonia instead
Normal observations support a self-limiting course

labs.test: Chest X-ray only if focal signs or over three weeks

conditions.name: Acute bronchitis

triage.label: Self-care
triage.action: This can usually be managed at home

conditions.summary: Viral inflammation of the airways, not the lung tissue. A cough that drags on for two to three weeks, sometimes with phlegm, but the patient is not systemically unwell.
workup: Chest X-ray only if focal signs or red flags

exam.step: Look for allergic shiners and a transverse nasal crease

labs.test: Specific IgE or skin prick testing
labs.confirms: Identifies the allergen if avoidance is planned

conditions.name: Allergic rhinitis

triage.label: Routine
triage.action: Discuss with your doctor at a routine appointment

conditions.summary: An allergic reaction in the nose. Sneezing fits, clear runny nose and itchy watery eyes, recurring in a season or around a specific trigger, and never with fever.
workup: Skin prick or specific IgE testing if unclear

exam.positive: Clear chest distinguishes it from pneumonia

labs.test: Clinical diagnosis during a known season

conditions.name: Influenza

triage.label: See a doctor soon
triage.action: Book an appointment in the next few days

conditions.summary: Abrupt high fever with severe muscle aches, headache and exhaustion that floors the patient within hours. Far more systemic than a common cold.
workup: Antivirals within 48 hours for at-risk groups
Chest X-ray if secondary pneumonia suspected

exam.step: Palpate over the maxillary and frontal sinuses

labs.test: CT sinuses only if complications or surgery planned

conditions.name: Acute sinusitis

triage.label: Self-care
triage.action: This can usually be managed at home

conditions.summary: Inflamed sinuses following a cold. Facial pressure worse on bending forward, a blocked nose and a reduced sense of smell, typically after day ten of a cold.
workup: Antibiotics only if severe or worsening after 10 days

exam.step: Pulse oximetry at rest and after exertion
exam.positive: A fall of 3% or more on exertion is significant

exam.step: Respiratory rate over a full minute

labs.test: FBC, CRP, renal function if unwell

conditions.name: COVID-19

triage.label: See a doctor soon
triage.action: Book an appointment in the next few days

conditions.summary: Coronavirus infection with a wide range of severity. Fever, dry cough and fatigue predominate; loss of smell or taste is the most specific pointer.

exam.step: Inspect the tonsils with a light

exam.positive: Absence of cough is a Centor criterion

labs.test: Throat swab if the rapid test is negative

conditions.name: Streptococcal pharyngitis

triage.label: See a doctor soon
triage.action: Book an appointment in the next few days

conditions.summary: Group A streptococcal throat infection. Fever with pus on the tonsils and tender neck glands, and pointedly no cough.
workup: Rapid antigen test or throat swab
Penicillin V ten days if score high

exam.positive: Hoarseness with an otherwise normal throat

labs.confirms: No test in the acute phase

labs.test: Urgent ENT referral if hoarse over three weeks

conditions.name: Acute laryngitis

triage.label: Self-care
triage.action: This can usually be managed at home

conditions.summary: Viral inflammation of the voice box. The voice drops to a croak or disappears, with a mild sore throat and a dry cough. Voice rest is the treatment.
workup: ENT referral if hoarseness persists beyond 3 weeks

labs.test: FBC, CRP, ESR, TFTs, coeliac, B12, ferritin, glucose
Diagnosis after symptoms exceed three months

conditions.name: Chronic fatigue syndrome / ME

triage.label: Routine
triage.action: Discuss with your doctor at a routine appointment

conditions.summary: Disabling fatigue lasting over three months with post-exertional worsening, unrefreshing sleep and cognitive difficulty, after other causes have been excluded.
workup: FBC, CRP, TFTs, coeliac, B12, ferritin, glucose

exam.positive: Posterior chain involvement is more suggestive than anterior
Present in about half; contraindicates contact sport
Marked tonsillar exudate with palatal petechiae

conditions.name: Infectious mononucleosis

triage.label: See a doctor soon
triage.action: Book an appointment in the next few days

conditions.summary: Epstein-Barr virus infection in a teenager or young adult. A severe sore throat with hugely swollen glands and a fatigue that outlasts everything else by weeks.
workup: FBC and film for atypical lymphocytes
Avoid contact sport for 4 weeks (splenic rupture risk)

exam.positive: The uvula is pushed away from the affected side
Difficulty opening the mouth is characteristic

labs.confirms: Needs aspiration or incision and drainage

labs.test: Do not delay referral for investigations

conditions.name: Peritonsillar abscess (quinsy)

triage.label: Emergency
triage.action: Call emergency services or go to an emergency department now

conditions.summary: A collection of pus beside a tonsil. Sore throat worsens to one side, the voice goes muffled, and the mouth will barely open. Needs drainage.
workup: Needle aspiration or incision and drainage

exam.positive: Examination can precipitate complete airway obstruction

labs.test: No investigation before the airway is secured

conditions.name: Epiglottitis

triage.label: Emergency
triage.action: Call emergency services or go to an emergency department now

conditions.summary: Infection swelling the flap above the voice box, which can close the airway within hours. Drooling, a muffled voice and sitting upright to breathe are the danger signs.
workup: Keep the patient upright and calm

redFlags.label: Possible sepsis
redFlags.message: A fever together with confusion, very fast breathing, mottled skin or a collapsing blood pressure can mean infection is affecting the whole body.
redFlags.action: Call emergency services now. Do not wait to see whether it settles.

redFlags.label: Rash that does not fade under pressure
redFlags.message: Spots that stay visible when a glass is pressed on them, alongside feeling unwell, can be a sign of bacteria in the bloodstream.

redFlags.label: Possible severe allergic reaction
redFlags.message: Swelling of the throat or tongue with difficulty breathing after a food, sting, or medicine can close the airway within minutes.
redFlags.action: Use an adrenaline auto-injector if you have one, then call emergency services.

redFlags.label: Reduced consciousness
redFlags.message: Being difficult to rouse, or drifting in and out of awareness, always needs immediate assessment whatever the cause.
redFlags.action: Call emergency services now. Place the person on their side if unresponsive.

redFlags.label: Possible stroke
redFlags.message: Sudden facial drooping, arm weakness or difficulty speaking is a stroke until proven otherwise. Treatment works only within a few hours.
redFlags.action: Call emergency services now and note the exact time symptoms began.

redFlags.label: Seizure
redFlags.message: A first seizure needs assessment to find the cause and to advise on driving and safety.
redFlags.action: Seek urgent assessment today. Call emergency services if the seizure lasted over five minutes or a second one followed.

redFlags.label: Significant gastrointestinal bleeding
redFlags.message: Vomiting blood, or passing black tarry stools, means bleeding inside the digestive tract.
redFlags.action: Go to an emergency department now.

redFlags.label: New jaundice
redFlags.message: Yellowing of the skin or eyes always needs blood tests to find out why.

redFlags.label: Sudden loss of vision
redFlags.message: Sight lost suddenly in one or both eyes needs assessment the same hour, whatever the cause.
redFlags.action: Go to an eye emergency department now.

redFlags.label: Sore throat with airway warning signs
redFlags.message: A sore throat with drooling, a muffled voice, or difficulty breathing may mean the airway is narrowing.
redFlags.action: Call emergency services now. Stay sitting upright and stay calm. Do not put anything in the mouth.

redFlags.label: Food sticking on swallowing
redFlags.message: Food that sticks going down, especially with weight loss, needs an urgent camera test of the gullet.
redFlags.action: Request an urgent endoscopy referral within two weeks.

redFlags.label: Thoughts of self-harm
redFlags.message: Thoughts of harming yourself or of being better off dead deserve help today. You do not have to be in crisis to reach out.
redFlags.action: Contact your doctor, a crisis line, or go to an emergency department now. If you are in immediate danger, call emergency services.

redFlags.label: New confusion coming on over hours or days
redFlags.message: Confusion that has come on over hours or days, or that comes and goes through the day, is delirium until proven otherwise. It is caused by something else -- an infection, a drug, pain, retention -- and that cause needs finding today.
redFlags.action: Seek same-day medical assessment. Take a list of all medications. Call emergency services if they are drowsy, feverish or cannot be roused properly.

disclaimer: This tool provides information about possible causes of symptoms. It is not a diagnosis and it cannot examine you. It does not replace assessment by a qualified clinician. If you feel very unwell, or your symptoms are getting rapidly worse, seek medical help immediately regardless of what this tool says.
